propositions: The byte-equivalence oracle executes a copied _legacy_convert subprocess 884 times in parallel with production _convert, but both read the same mutable _PANDOC_TO constant, making the oracle non-independent and unable to detect production format mutations.

The immutable golden-output fixture replaces the copied Pandoc subprocess with deterministic expected bytes, reducing test runtime from 65.5s to 33.1s (884 eliminated subprocesses) while preserving all 884 real production conversions.
Patchset 1 fixture schema stored a single macOS-arm64 Pandoc binary SHA-256 without platform mapping, causing Ubuntu CI to reject the same version under a different Linux x86_64 binary hash.

Patchset 2 adds a complete platform-keyed fingerprint map (darwin-arm64 and linux-x86_64), selecting the exact supported hash by stable platform/architecture; unknown platforms and version/hash mismatches fail with diagnostics.

All 884 prepared corpus units continue through production _convert and real Pandoc on every per-change run; the fixture regeneration command is documented and deterministic, reproducing the 464,245-byte fixture byte-identically.

A defect-seeded mutation of production format to plain makes the independent oracle RED, and the complete-map version-plus-binary-fingerprint assertion fails on platform/hash drift, with held-out behavioral tests covering both platforms.
